signal: Fiery launched several products in 2026 including JobFlow Pro, FS700 Pro, and a custom DFE platform with Xerox, expanding across production and textile print

email.body1:
Nick, saw Fiery shipped a wave of launches this year, JobFlow Pro, FS700 Pro, and the custom Xerox DFE platform.

That many launches usually means more inbound and signals than the SDR team can follow up on fast enough, so good leads cool while reps grind through research and CRM. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so each rep covers far more without longer ramp: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to three of Fiery's top target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through them?
email.body2:
Nick, quick follow-up for Fiery.

When launches stack up, response speed and follow-up consistency are usually where SDR pipeline leaks, and it is hard to see exactly where. Our built-in best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I would change to get reps to first meeting faster.
email.body3:
Nick, last bit of proof for Fiery.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your SDR team's reply rate likely compares to other software vendors. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Nick, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If speeding up follow-up without adding SDR headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A heavy launch calendar keeps an SDR team plenty busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your SDR team? I will tailor it to Fiery either way.
